captions.detailed: This 3D model is a double-ended socket wrench tool. It consists of a flat, rectangular handle with circular, rounded heads on both ends. Protruding vertically from the top center of each circular head is a square drive peg, with one peg significantly larger than the other. The entire wrench is a solid, single-piece design with smooth flat surfaces and vertical circular edges.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric double-ended socket wrench in OpenSCAD. The user should be able to configure the tool length, thickness, handle width, and the drive sizes on both ends (such as 1/4" and 1/2") including a custom tolerance factor for the square drive pegs.
captions.factory: The socket wrench is built using a union of the main handle body and the two drive pegs. The body is constructed by placing two cylinders at either end of the handle span, and connecting them with a central rectangular cube. The square socket drives are created using cube primitives, scaled according to the user-defined drive sizes minus a tolerance parameter, translated to sit on top of the circular ends of the handle.
